citeAs: Davis AP, Wiegers TC, Sciaky D, Barkalow F, Strong M, Wyatt B, Wiegers J, McMorran R, Abrar S, Mattingly CJ Comparative Toxicogenomics Database’s 20th anniversary: update 2025. Nucleic Acids Res. 2024 Oct 10.
conditionsOfAccess: The Comparative Toxicogenomics DatabaseTM (CTDTM) is provided to enhance knowledge and encourage progress in the scientific community. It is to be used only for research and educational purposes. Medical treatment decisions should not be made based on the information in CTD.
dct:provenance:
Metadata was generated solely from CTD pages under the configured authoritative source and from the files directly advertised by https://ctdbase.org/downloads/; no GitHub or other public repository was used.
The crawl downloaded all 67 unique /reports/ assets advertised by the live Data Downloads page. No advertised report branch failed traversal or download. The external Exposure Ontology registry link was treated as contextual navigation rather than a CTD-hosted release asset.
RecordSets were generated for 42 CSV/TSV assets. In every such file, the source declares exact machine column tokens in a commented '# Fields:' block rather than an in-band header row; those tokens were preserved character-for-character. Datatype inference used at most five data rows and remained conservative. Four exposure CSV/TSV schemas and their rows have a trailing delimiter after the final named field; the resulting unnamed, uniformly empty position was omitted rather than assigned an invented placeholder. XML, XSD, and OBO assets are distributions but do not receive invented column mappings.
Files ending in .gz are compressed single files, not archives, and therefore have no inner-file distribution entries. Their encodingFormat describes gzip compression; their RecordSet schemas were inspected after streaming decompression without changing the downloaded originals.
CTD states custom research/education and commercial-use terms but does not identify a canonical standard license or version after checking its homepage, download, legal, publication/citation, and FAIRness pages; license is therefore the required literal 'Not Found'. conditionsOfAccess quotes the legal page verbatim.
The current release is identified by CTD as July 2026 and the live page reports data updated July 1, 2026; this is represented as version and dateModified. No distinct authoritative original-publication date was found, so datePublished is omitted.
The human-readable download page labels some fields with display punctuation and capitalization that differ from the exact machine schemas (for example, 'City,Town,Region,Area' versus 'citytownregionarea'); machine tokens govern field.name and source.extract.column.
Two additive GeoCoordinates parents group the coherent studycountries, stateorprovince, and citytownregionarea columns in the CSV and TSV exposure-event RecordSets. Their normalized addressCountry, addressRegion, and addressLocality subfield labels explicitly map back to the unchanged exact source selectors. The exposure-study files contain studycountries alone; a single broad, multi-valued country field was not forced into a location hierarchy without region/locality or coordinate support.
description: CTD is a robust, publicly available database that aims to advance understanding about how environmental exposures affect human health.
